input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving parity

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: whether vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators reaches functional and performance parity with the productized CUDA builds for the platform's supported model set. It runs a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware and produces the parity data plus a recommended go/no-go productization scope per model — the outcome that determines the scope of the vLLM ROCm serving runtime productization. The epic's scope also includes securing access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or partner-lab arrangement).

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct hardware for the campaign (procurement or partner-lab); the granting of access is externally controlled and tracked as a risk, while everything the campaign produces is within this epic's control.
- Define the validation matrix: the supported model set, functional pass/fail criteria per model, and the performance parity baselines measured against the productized CUDA runtime builds.
- Execute vLLM serving validation on ROCm for every model in the supported model set, using upstream ROCm-enabled vLLM builds.
- Measure performance parity data per model against the CUDA baseline.
- Publish the campaign report: per-model functional results, performance parity data, and a recommended go/no-go productization scope for each validated model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation plan exists that enumerates the supported model set, the functional pass/fail criteria, and the performance parity baselines against the CUDA runtime builds.
- The campaign report is published with functional validation results for every model in the supported model set.
- The campaign report includes performance parity data per model, measured against the CUDA baseline on comparable hardware.
- The campaign report states a recommended go/no-go productization scope for each validated model.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): full coverage — the validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, and producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks

- Hardware access (procurement or partner-lab) is unresolved and controlled by parties outside the strategy; it may delay the campaign but does not change the campaign's deliverables.
- Upstream ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; the campaign validates against the upstream ROCm builds available at execution time.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by the validation campaign, as an additional runtime variant alongside the existing CUDA builds. It delivers the midstream ROCm runtime image and the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime resources that make the runtime deployable through KServe InferenceServices on AMD Instinct nodes.

## Scope

- Build and maintain the vLLM ROCm runtime image as a new image variant in the existing vLLM midstream repo (the repo is already onboarded; no new repo creation is needed).
- Productize the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime resources for the ROCm vLLM runtime, covering exactly the model set cleared by the validation campaign.
- Build the ROCm runtime image from a supported upstream ROCm base aligned to the platform release train.
- Validate KServe InferenceServices deploying and serving with the ROCm runtime on AMD Instinct nodes — KServe itself requires no code change for this strategy, so this is validation of a passive component rather than KServe development.
- Build the image through the platform build pipeline (Konflux); the pipeline onboarding for the ROCm image variant runs in parallel with this epic, and this epic's completion is gated by a green pipeline run rather than by a dependency on the pipeline work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The vLLM ROCm runtime image is built and green through the platform build pipeline (Konflux).
- ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime resources for the ROCm vLLM runtime are productized for exactly the model set cleared by the validation campaign.
- A KServe InferenceService using the ROCm vLLM runtime deploys and serves inference requests on AMD Instinct hardware.
- The ROCm vLLM runtime ships as a supported runtime variant in a platform release, alongside (not replacing) the existing CUDA runtime builds.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): full coverage — a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime productized for the models the validation campaign clears.
- This epic also carries the validation of KServe (listed as an affected component with no code change implied), per the third acceptance criterion.

## Risks

- Scope is gated on the validation campaign outcome: if fewer models clear than expected, productization narrows to the cleared set; if no model clears, productization is halted and the outcome is reported back to the strategy.
- Upstream ROCm runtime image cadence is controlled by AMD and may not align with platform release trains; a supported upstream base that is not release-train-aligned delays the release but does not change this epic's scope.

# Konflux build pipeline for the vLLM ROCm runtime image

## Description

This epic onboards the new vLLM ROCm runtime container image to the platform build pipeline (Konflux), so the ROCm variant is built, tested, and released through the same pipeline as the existing CUDA runtime builds of the already-onboarded vLLM midstream repo.

## Scope

- Add the ROCm image variant to the Konflux pipeline configuration for the existing vLLM midstream repo (known-recipe onboarding; the repo is already Konflux-onboarded, so this extends the existing pipeline to the new image variant).
- Ensure the pipeline builds, tests, and scans the ROCm runtime image and produces its artifacts per platform version, alongside the CUDA variants.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Konflux pipeline configuration builds the vLLM ROCm runtime image from the existing midstream repo.
- A pipeline run for the ROCm image variant is green across its build, test, and scan stages.
- The ROCm image variant is produced per platform version alongside the existing CUDA variants.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0) — enabling coverage: this epic provides the build-pipeline leg of the productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime. It runs in parallel with the runtime productization work; their coupling is expressed as the "build pipeline green" acceptance criterion on that epic, not as a dependency between them.

# PyTorch ROCm training support for PyTorchJob

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on ROCm for jobs run through the Training Operator: PyTorchJob workloads executing on AMD Instinct nodes with ROCm-enabled PyTorch training images, in single-GPU and multi-GPU job topologies, admitted through the platform's queueing layer.

## Scope

- Support PyTorchJob execution on AMD Instinct nodes using ROCm-enabled PyTorch training images (single-GPU and multi-GPU topologies).
- Validate the job lifecycle for ROCm-based PyTorchJobs (creation, run to completion, status reporting, cleanup).
- Validate multi-GPU distributed training jobs on ROCm end to end, admitted through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota configured (the quota configuration itself is delivered by the queueing workstream; this epic validates the training jobs against it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob runs to completion on AMD Instinct nodes using a ROCm-enabled PyTorch image.
- A multi-GPU distributed PyTorchJob runs to completion on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Multi-GPU PyTorchJobs are admitted through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota handling, using the queueing layer's AMD GPU quota configuration.
- Job conditions and status are reported correctly for ROCm-based PyTorchJobs, consistent with existing GPU-backed jobs.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): training side — PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs.

## Risks

- Validation requires access to AMD Instinct hardware; the availability of dedicated nodes is controlled by parties outside the strategy (shared constraint with the serving validation campaign) and may delay validation but does not change this epic's deliverables.

# Kueue quota handling for amd.com/gpu

## Description

This epic extends the platform's queueing and orchestration layer so that queued workloads requesting AMD GPUs are admitted with amd.com/gpu quota handling: quota and resource-flavor configuration covering AMD Instinct accelerators for single- and multi-GPU jobs, consistent with the existing quota model for other accelerators.

## Scope

- Define and support quota/resource-flavor configuration for amd.com/gpu in the Kueue ClusterQueue/LocalQueue model, so administrators can allocate AMD Instinct capacity to queues.
- Validate admission of workloads requesting amd.com/gpu, including all-or-nothing (gang) admission semantics for multi-GPU and multi-node job topologies.
- Validate that quota behavior for amd.com/gpu (admission, pending on quota exhaustion, accounting) is consistent with the existing GPU quota behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted through Kueue quota configured for AMD Instinct accelerators.
- All-or-nothing (gang) admission works for multi-GPU jobs requesting amd.com/gpu.
- Quota exhaustion for amd.com/gpu leaves workloads pending (not failed), consistent with existing GPU quota behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): queueing side — single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota handling.

## Risks

- Validation requires access to AMD Instinct hardware; the availability of dedicated nodes is controlled by parties outside the strategy (shared constraint with the serving validation campaign) and may delay validation but does not change this epic's deliverables.

# AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement documentation

## Description

This epic documents AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement in the platform documentation: the supported AMD hardware and driver prerequisites, the validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, and the PyTorch ROCm training support with amd.com/gpu quota usage. It is authored after the implementation work so the content describes what was actually built and validated.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Supported AMD hardware: the AMD Instinct accelerators on which ROCm serving and training are supported, and the driver prerequisites (including the GPU operator/driver requirements for AMD nodes).
- The validated model list for vLLM ROCm serving, matching the scope cleared by the validation campaign.
- PyTorch training on ROCm: supported single- and multi-GPU job shapes and how jobs are submitted and admitted through Kueue.
- amd.com/gpu quota usage: how administrators configure queues for AMD Instinct capacity and how users request AMD GPUs.
- Any platform prerequisites or constraints for AMD GPU nodes, stated at the level the implementation work validated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics state the supported AMD hardware and driver prerequisites.
- Documentation states the validated model list, matching the scope cleared by the validation campaign.
- Documentation covers PyTorch ROCm training support, including single- and multi-GPU jobs and Kueue admission with amd.com/gpu quota.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented and validated capabilities (serving runtime, build pipeline, training, quota handling) before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): full coverage — documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list.

## Notes

- The strategy names no documentation owner; this epic is assigned to the serving team as the strategy's primary owner. Content spans both the serving and training areas, so technical reviewers should include the training/queueing team.
